title: 2026-12-09 POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Went over networking blockers, routing + NAT issues, recent runtime upgrade plan, and initial throughput/latency numbers from benchmark runs. Agreed on an upgrade window next week, SE will send firewall rule checklist and updated benchmark script; customer to run a 2-hour run and share logs. Security team requested SOC2 docs and KMS integration guide.
topics: networking: VPC peering and route tables
action_items: Devon Park - share firewall/security-group checklist + sample CloudFormation/Terraform rules - due 2026-12-11
Priya Shah - run 2-hour throughput run with beam-8 config and upload logs to shared S3 - due 2026-12-14
Ava Martinez - send updated pricing sheet and pilot addendum; include burst capacity pricing - due 2026-12-10
Elena Gomez - confirm KMS key rotation policy questions and share compliance contact - due 2026-12-13
Devon Park - schedule maintenance/upgrade window for runtime 1.4.0 with rollback plan - proposed 2026-12-16
next_steps: SE to provide firewall checklist and sample IaC
Customer to run targeted 2-hour benchmark and upload artifacts
Redwood to prepare upgrade runbook and rollback steps
Security docs (SOC2, KMS integration) to be shared via secure link
Schedule final verification call after benchmark (week of 12/15)
transcript: [00:00] Ava (Redwood AE): Hey everyone good morning, thanks for joining. We're on for about 55 minutes, agenda is quick network blockers, results from last week's perf run, and plan to roll the runtime upgrade. Who's on from Nimbus?
[00:08] Priya (Nimbus SRE): Hey Ava, Priya here. Markus, Elena and Tom are with me. Morning all.
[00:12] Markus (Nimbus): Morning. We hit one pretty annoying routing issue after the NAT change so hoping to walk through that.

[00:20] Devon (Redwood SE): Cool, I captured that. Quick note: I'll share a firewall SG checklist and an example Terraform later in the call. First let's hit the perf numbers you ran yesterday, Priya?

[00:30] Priya (Nimbus SRE): Yeah so we did a 30 minute run with batch size 8, beam-ish config, default KV cache off on the first run and then enabled. Initial p50 was around 110 ms per token, p95 around 360ms. When KV cache was _on_ p50 dropped to ~85ms, p95 to 220ms but we saw memory pressure on the instance around 54 minutes in, so we killed before the full hour.

[00:55] Devon (Redwood SE): That memory pressure lines up with the older runtime (1.3.2) memory leak we patched in 1.4.0. Good catch. Could you share the logs? The heap growth pattern helps us validate the fix.
[01:05] Priya (Nimbus SRE): Yep uploading the logs to the S3 bucket you shared - link is in the chat. There's also a grep of OOM lines, might be noisy.
[01:12] Ava (Redwood AE): Thanks. Markus, you mentioned a NAT/eip change?

[01:16] Markus (Nimbus): We rotated the NAT gateway to consolidate egress. After rotation, connections from the private subnet to Redwood control plane intermittently failed — looks like route table entries didn't update or there was a stateful firewall blocking the new egress IP.

[01:30] Tom (Dev): For clarity, we use VPC peering to Redwood Private and also rely on a proxy (squid) for egress, so when the NAT changed the proxy saw different source IPs and our firewall policy dropped traffic mid-stream.

[01:45] Devon (Redwood SE): Understood. Two things to check: route tables for the Redwood peering subnet (sometimes the peering route didn't propagate), and firewall rules keyed to old EIP. I'll prepare an itemized checklist. Also note Redwood's control plane accepts TLS client certs but the data plane is tunneled through the VPC connector; we need the egress to be stable during downloads of model shards.
[02:10] Elena (Nimbus Security): Quick security question — how do you handle KMS keys for model encryption in Redwood Private? We need to map to our internal HSM onboarding checklist.

[02:18] Devon (Redwood SE): We support customer-managed KMS; you can bring your own key (BYOK) and we integrate via standard KMS APIs. For on-prem HSM we'll share the integration guide — there's a minor step that requires key wrapping for the model artifacts. I'll drop the doc.

[02:36] Priya (Nimbus SRE): Perfect. Back to perf: we saw GPU utilization hit ~92% with KV cache enabled and token throughput flattened, which suggests the runtime was bottlenecked on memory bandwidth at that run-length. Did you want us to test different quantization or smaller batch sizes?

[02:50] Devon (Redwood SE): Good data. For the next run please try two variants: keep KV cache but reduce batch to 6, and a second run with runtime 1.4.0 candidate image that includes the memory leak fix and kernel selection improvements. That will isolate whether it's the runtime or batch config.
[03:05] Priya (Nimbus SRE): Noted — we can schedule the 2-hour run and tag the artifacts. Any special flags we should set?

[03:10] Devon (Redwood SE): Use the --perf-trace flag and capture docker stats and /proc/meminfo every 30s. We'll add a script in the shared repo. Also enable KV cache TTL at 30s for the run so we can see eviction behavior.

[03:25] Ava (Redwood AE): Quick sales note — because the pilot is expanding, I'll include burst pricing options and an updated pilot addendum. We'll keep the pilot cap but allow a one-time burst window for the 2-hour run.

[03:35] Markus (Nimbus): That works. One blocker for us is the firewall change window — we need an explicit rollback plan. If you upgrade runtime and the model-shard download fails we need to revert to 1.3.2 quickly.

[03:45] Devon (Redwood SE): Absolutely. Our proposed upgrade window is a 45-minute window with canary on 1 node, metrics monitored: token latency, error rate, memory, and model shard download time. Rollback is immediate: redeploy 1.3.2 image to the pool. I'll add the exact commands to the runbook.
[04:05] Elena (Nimbus Security): Also need to confirm audit logging. Does Redwood Private produce per-request audit logs that we can ship to our SIEM?
[04:12] Lila (Redwood CSM): Yes, we can stream audit logs from the control plane to your S3 or Syslog endpoint; we also have a retention policy template. We'll share the doc link in chat.
[04:22] Tom (Dev): The model catalog sync failed last night too — probably related to the egress IP change. The agent couldn't pull the v1.2 -> v1.3 model bundle. We had to trigger a manual download.

[04:31] Devon (Redwood SE): That matches the egress IP issue. If you whitelist the new EIP range or use the VPC peering route we sent, downloads should succeed. I'll include the exact CIDR ranges and sample iptables rules in the checklist.

[05:00] Priya (Nimbus SRE): One small thing: we noticed the label on the runtime image in your docs is 1.4.0-rc, but the image in the registry had a slightly different tag (1.4.0-rc2) — confusion there. Can you confirm the canonical tag to pull?

[05:10] Devon (Redwood SE): Good catch — that's on us. The canonical tag should be redwood/inference:1.4.0-rc. We'll reconcile registry tags and update the docs; I'll also push a digest pin so you can avoid tag drift.
[05:20] Ava (Redwood AE): Taking note — I'll send the explicit link to the digest in the follow-up email. Any open questions on compliance or SOC2?

[05:28] Elena (Nimbus Security): We need the SOC2 Type II report and a short answer on data residency — our compliance team wants to ensure logs and model artifacts stay in the us-east-1 S3 bucket and don't replicate globally.

[05:38] Lila (Redwood CSM): We have a SOC2 package in the repo, and we can provide a signed ATO letter for the pilot. On data residency, Redwood Private running in your VPC keeps artifacts in your S3; we'll make sure replication is disabled. I'll share the compliance packet link.

[05:50] Priya (Nimbus SRE): Great. About the test plan: we'll run the two variants Devon suggested — batch 6 + KV, and runtime 1.4.0 with batch 8 — each for 1 hour, but we'll do a 2-hour run to get steady-state data. We'll collect perf traces and docker stats as asked.
[06:05] Devon (Redwood SE): Excellent. When you upload, please include the perf-trace tarball and a simple CSV of p50/p95 numbers per minute. That lets us plot the trend and correlate with memory.
[06:12] Priya (Nimbus SRE): Will do. Also curious about quantization — is your recommendation to stay on int8 for production or float16? We saw a slight quality delta in our evals.

[06:20] Devon (Redwood SE): For now float16 preserves quality best; int8 is cost-optimized but may need a small calibration step for this model family. We'll share a short eval harness so you can run a quality vs latency sweep. We'll include the recommended quantization profile per model.
[06:35] Markus (Nimbus): From an ops perspective we also want to know autoscale behavior under burst — how quickly can Redwood Dedicated or Private add capacity if we trigger an emergency surge?

[06:45] Ava (Redwood AE): For Private deployments autoscaling is constrained by your pool; we can recommend a burst pool config that pre-spins warm instances. For Dedicated we have pre-reserved capacity that can autoscale faster. I'll include burst config options in the pricing addendum.
[06:55] Tom (Dev): One more networking nuance: do you support static egress IPs for model shard downloads if we want to avoid firewall churn?
[07:00] Devon (Redwood SE): Yes, you can configure NAT with Elastic IPs or use a dedicated egress gateway. We'll document the pattern and pros/cons. Static EIP is simplest for firewall rules.
[07:10] Elena (Nimbus Security): Good. Regarding KMS: what's the rotation cadence and do you support import-only keys?

[07:16] Devon (Redwood SE): We support customer-managed keys with rotation policies; import-only keys are supported but require an HSM onboarding step. I'll have our cryptography doc included in the security packet.

[07:28] Ava (Redwood AE): Okay let's capture next steps — Devon you'll send the firewall checklist and runbook, Lila you'll share SOC2 + compliance packet, I'll send pricing and pilot addendum. Priya you'll schedule the 2-hour run and upload artifacts. Any objections?
[07:40] Priya (Nimbus SRE): No objections, just need the window for the run, likely 12/14 afternoon for us — I'll sync with Markus and propose a time.

[07:48] Ava (Redwood AE): Sounds good. We'll tentatively aim for 12/14 14:00 ET. If the run looks good we'll plan the upgrade window for 12/16 for the 1.4.0 rollout with the canary approach. Devon will provide rollback commands.
[08:00] Devon (Redwood SE): I'll also include a small script to automate canary promotion and rollback to make the maintenance deterministic. Expect the doc in the shared drive by EOD tomorrow.
[08:12] Tom (Dev): Quick note: I'll also add a monitoring dashboard for model-shard download latency and track token-level latency per pod so we can quickly triage regressions during the canary.

[08:20] Elena (Nimbus Security): And I'll review the KMS doc; if we need an exception we'll flag it early. Also please provide the precise retention period on audit logs so our legal team can sign off.
[08:30] Lila (Redwood CSM): Retention options are configurable; default is 90 days, we can extend per request — will include that in the packet.
[08:40] Ava (Redwood AE): Great. Any final questions?
[08:44] Markus (Nimbus): Just one: competitor question — if we run into more issues, what would the typical escalation to engineering look like? We may need deeper help beyond SE.

[08:52] Ava (Redwood AE): We have an escalation path: SE -> Staff SE -> Eng on-call, and for enterprise pilots we can open a named support channel. I'll add the escalation contacts in the follow-up as well.
[09:00] Priya (Nimbus SRE): Perfect. We'll run the tests and get back with logs. Thanks everyone.
[09:05] Devon (Redwood SE): Thanks, we'll follow up with the checklist and runbook. Bye.
[09:08] Ava (Redwood AE): Bye all, talk soon.
